title: Grateful Dead Live at Hollywood Bowl on 1967-09-15
lineage: AUD > MC > R > R > NR > DAT > CDR > EAC (secure) > Cool Edit (remove isolated pops) > mkwACT > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: Crude, drop‑out‑laden audience recording, yet the 9/15/67 Hollywood Bowl show dazzles with Jerry’s scorching leads, Pigpen’s organ/harmonica fire, and standout jams on Viola Lee Blues, Alligator and more.
ai_review.review: The performance captures a top‑form Dead in late ’67 – Jerry and Pigpen trading solos, Phil’s fretless bass thumping, and psychedelic extensions that make songs like Viola Lee Blues, Alligator and Morning Dew shine. The audience (AUD) source is riddled with hiss, drop‑outs and a rough mix, which many listeners find distracting, but the energy and historic vibe of the show often outweigh the technical flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance while repeatedly criticizing the audio quality; weighting show strength (70%) against recording issues (30%) yields a solid above‑average rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crude, low‑fidelity AUD tape with frequent drop‑outs, hiss and intrusive crowd chatter; mix is thin but captures the era's ambience.

standout_songs: Beat It On Down The Line
show_quality.setlist_flow: A typical late‑1967 set with long psychedelic jams and high energy; the band rides a loose, improvisational groove that builds excitement despite occasional uneven pacing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for fiery, full‑hog guitar work and tight control during jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for thumping fretless bass that underpins the performance.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ (and occasional harmonica) highlighted as a key element giving the show its 1960s vibe.
